entities.title: zazzle flow and zazzle review
entities.summary: The repository workflow zazzle runs for an agent, opt-in per repository with .zazzle/flow.json: preview, verify with tree-pinned receipts, write the commit message, changelog entry or pull request text, deliver (stage, commit, push, pull request) safely repeatable, test-first delegation, a single CI wait, and a multi-viewpoint review that fixes what it finds before handing back.
entities.purpose: mod.rs parses `flow SUBCOMMAND` (and `review`, which the launcher and the daemon's command line route here) and resolves the agents: the ladder from --agents, agents.ladder or the installed local models; the writer, reviewers, final reviewer, fixer and test author from flags, then the policy, then the ladder. policy.rs reads the opt-in file or discovers the projects' checks, gives each branch a review level, and compares what the guidance says about pull request targets. repo.rs wraps git: the working tree's tree through a temporary index that keeps the real index's modification time, diffs, bases and restoring paths. verify.rs runs the applicable checks and keeps receipts and logs in the git directory keyed by tree. write.rs drafts and validates prose with a cheap writer. deliver.rs stages exactly the named paths and reuses a commit, push or open pull request a retry finds. ci.rs waits on gh for the head's checks. edit.rs is how agents change files (hosted agents edit with no shell; local models return whole files), reverting anything outside their scope. testfirst.rs accepts a test only when it fails for the stated reason, then lets the fixer change production paths only. review.rs picks viewpoints by level and signals, briefs, reviews, adjudicates, remediates and re-reviews, keeping a ledger per branch. docs.rs has the cheap writer (never the executor) bring the READMEs and .dev records beside and above the changed files in step, limited to documentation paths, checked for valid JSON and by the repository's docs checks, undone if they keep failing. tidy.rs runs the format and lint checks' fix commands, re-checks, and hands leftover lint to the local agent; review remediation and test-first run the format fixes after each agent edit. mod.rs's TOOLS_NOTE tells every execution agent that formatting, linting, builds, tests, coverage, documentation, prose and CI waits are zazzle's. coverage.rs runs the coverage checks, reads lcov, Cobertura, Go, coverage.py or llvm-cov reports into per-file gaps for the changed files with the tests to model on, and lets a cheap author write tests for them, kept only if every coverage check still passes. ci.rs also fetches failed jobs' logs through gh, cuts them to the error lines, and has the local model triage each failure (test, place, cause, owner, next step). audit.rs runs the dependency audits that apply, lists their advisories and runs their fix commands on request. update.rs merges the target into the branch, regenerates conflicted lockfiles, has the local agent resolve other conflicts, and commits only when no marker is left and the checks pass, aborting otherwise. generate.rs runs the generators whose inputs changed and reports or puts back stale outputs; generated outputs are kept from agents and reviews. headers.rs checks and adds license headers in each file's comment style. A complex branch update is reviewed by the strongest agent before it is committed, and any error after a merge starts undoes it; deliver.rs's merge_pr merges a pull request only when the policy allows it, its head's checks are green and no review finding is open.
boundaries: Delivery needs the opt-in file and only has the effects it lists; protected and higher-level branches are refused.
A push that the remote rejects is reported, never forced.
Agents never run commands: hosted agents get Read, Grep, Glob (and Edit, Write when they may edit); zazzle runs every check itself.
Receipts, logs, drafts and ledgers live in .git/zazzle and are never committed.
Documentation is written by the writer, kept to documentation paths; code fixers may not touch it.
A branch update merges and never rebases or forces; it commits only a merge whose checks pass and aborts otherwise.
Merging is zazzle's (flow update, flow merge); agents only review complex merges. Pull requests are merged only when the policy lists the merge effect.
